HON. RENATO S. MUNEZ Municipal Vice Mayor La Paz, Agusan del Sur Dear Vice Mayor Munez: DILG Legal Opinion No. 44 s. 2012 JUL 1 0 2012 ßovesu ENT CENTRAL SIE"TuRE: DATE'. TINE: This pertains to your letter addressed to Chairman Maria Gracia Pulido-Tan of the Commission on Audit which was indorsed by Ms. Lita E. Diez, Head Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit, COA, to this Department, regarding the Appropriation Ordinance which the Sangguniang Bayan of La Paz, Agusan del Sur enacted but which was vetoed by the Honorable Mayor. Per your letter, the Sangguniang Bayan of La Paz, Agusan del Sur disapproved the IF (Intelligence Funds) budget because it did not follow the DILG MC No. 99-65, dated April 23, 1999 entitled Revised Guidelines Relative to the Utilization of funds for Intelligence or Confidential purposes and the letter of DILG Asec. Rolando M. Acosta (former Director of BLGS, DILG) to Chairman Reynaldo A. Villar, COA dated August 29, 2008 which provides the following: I) If no funds are allocated for peace and order concerns, it is understood that there is no need to utilize funds for intelligence purposes; 2) That to determine the amount to be utilized for intelligence and confidential purposes, it shall be based on (a) 30% of the peace and order allocations, or (b.) 3% of the annual appropriation whichever is lower. (emphasis supplied) Hence, you are now in a quandary on whether the previous year's budget on IF be re-enacted when it violated the DILG MC 3 99-65 on the ground that no allocation for peace and other concerns was appropriated. In reply thereto, we answer in the negative. In support, may we invite your attention to the following provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) which provides and we quote: "SECTION 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the Sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance

authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. However onl the annual a ro riations for salaries and wa of existing positions statutory and contractual obligations. and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of fimds shall be in accordance therewith. In the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concerned shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. xxx xxx (Emphasis Supplied) " ART. 415. Budget Authorization. xxx In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted. xxx Only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. xxx The aforequoted provisions clearly provide the consequence in case the Sanggunian fails to enact the annual appropriations, that is, the budget of the preceding year is reenacted. In case of reenacted budget, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted. This was reiterated by the Supreme Court in the case of Villanueva vs. Oplel. Accordingly, in a reenacted budget, there will be no creation of positions, no filling of positions, no new programs, projects and activities, the increase in Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) allocation for the year cannot be utilized since the same is not covered by an Appropriation Ordinance, and non-recurring activities cannot be undertaken no matter how vital they may be. In addition thereto, item II-I and 11-2 of DILG Memorandum Circular also provides that: "1. An allocation for peace and order concerns may be provided in the annual budget of a local government unit. Provided, that peace and order is a priority investment area; Funds for Intelligence or Confidential purposes may be 2. sourced from the: (a) appropriations for peace and order; or (b) total annual appropriations. Provided, that the total annual amount appropriated for Intelligence or Confidential undertakings shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the total annual amount 1 . No. 165125, 18 November 2005. GR.

allocated for peace and order efforts or three percent (3%) of the total annual appropriations, whichever is lower." In view thereof, since there was no allocation for peace and order concerns under a reenacted budget, the intelligence Funds (IF) therefore is not included in the reenacted items. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, Direc 111 LS:94/11
